name: Epie
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 2 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Thomas, Elaine & Kay Williamson. 1967. Wordlists of Delta Edo: Epie, Engenni, Degema. (Occasional Publication No. 8.) Ibadan: Institute of African Studies, University of Ibadan. 110 pp. [ERIC microfiche ED 158 582; archive.org item]
catalog_locator: Section '2. EPIE' (book p. 9), Phonology (c) tone and (d) syllable structure, book p. 11 = verb tone groups on book p. 12
catalog_quote: (c) The tone system has provisionally been treated as a terraced-level one. Low, as the most common tone, is left unmarked, high is marked /´/ and step /¯/. Extensive tone changes take place, as appears from a comparison of compounds with their component items. Glides have been written as a sequence of two tones on doubled vowels, but a deeper analysis might show that it was simpler to treat them as compressed sequences of tones on a single vowel, as in Engenni and Degema. (d) Syllable structures are simple: V, CV or N.
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

new_statements.rule_in_words: Epie is described as a terraced-level tone language (low, high, downstepped high; contour glides on long/doubled vowels). The description says nothing about word stress or accent; no stress rule can be extracted.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. Tone: 'extensive tone changes' in compounds; verbs sorted into three tone-pattern groups in the progressive; analysis explicitly 'provisional'.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical tone marked on citation forms in a wordlist; the phonology notes are a brief introduction (about two pages) covering both the Atissa (speaker marked A.) and Epie (E.) dialects as spoken at Yenagoa.
new_statements.identity_note: Thomas & Williamson 1967 describe Epie as spoken at Yenagoa, pooling two speakers: Mr. Otobo (Atissa clan, forms marked A.) and Mr. N. W. Gwegwe (Epie clan, marked E.); both dialects fall under Glottolog epie1238 (Epie-Atissa, ISO epi). The phonology notes are not dialect-specific except /k/ > [ɣ] as C2 in Atissa.

sources.note: Epie phonology section (book pp. 10-11, pp. 17-18) gives consonants, 9-vowel harmony system, tone ('provisionally.. terraced-level': low unmarked, high, step; glides = two tones on doubled vowels) and syllable structure V/CV/N. Nothing at all on stress or accent (page read visually; scanned of whole volume has no 'stress'/'accent'). Verb tone classes given by tone pattern in the progressive.
